title: Indivisible Sacramento & Friends Virtual Phone Bank!
description:
Sister District Sacramento’s Phone Bank, THE PHONOMENALS, is a cohesive group of dedicated callers most of whom have worked together for the past 5 years. We have a collective wealth of experience in talking with voters and are pleased to share that expertise and mentor all newcomers to our group.

Let’s keep Virginia blue!

Join Indivisible Sacramento on Wednesday 2:30pm-5:00pm PDT and., starting in July, Saturday 11:00am-1:00pm PDT.

...to help our candidate, Michael Feggans, keep Virginia blue! In 2023 Michael flipped House District 97 from red to blue in one of VA’s most competitive races. He is a staunch advocate for protecting reproductive rights, supporting public education, and advancing veterans' issues.

Virginia is having a general election in 2025, and keeping the majority in the House of Delegates is crucial.

After flipping the VA House of Delegates in 2023 by 975 votes, we must protect our Democratic majority to continue safeguarding democracy, especially with the growing threats coming from the federal government. Keeping the Dem majority ensures that Virginia remains a firewall against right-wing extremism and a leader in expanding economic opportunity, protecting freedoms, and defending democracy. A strong performance in Virginia this year will not only protect and expand the rights of Virginians but also generate national momentum, inspiring Democratic successes in the 2026 midterms.

This year Virginians will also be choosing their four top governing officials: Governor, Lt Governor, Secretary of State and Attorney General. As public interest is usually higher during gubernatorial elections, this provides us an opportunity to reach more voters, educate them around the importance of their state legislature and direct their attention to our candidate down ballot.

Why phonebank: The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. We provide our candidate’s campaign critical information about the district’s constituents which can then influence the campaign’s allocation of resources.

Come one, come all: No experience necessary. We offer individual training via Zoom prior to your first phone bank session as well as continued training, mentoring and support during each session. Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

description:
Help Michael Feggans win re-election while testing your knowledge of random facts all in the cozy confines of a gorgeous community space.

Trivia questions will be flying from a phenomenal Whaddyaknow? Trivia announcer.

Space is limited so be one of the lucky ones to join Sister District Greater Chicago at Schoolhouse Portage Park. 

Register a team of 5 *or* sign up and get assigned to a team! Either way *you'll have a blast*. Light snacks + a couple drinks included. 

Registration requires a minimum $50 donation per person. [Donate here to secure your spot(s)!](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sd038-va-feggans-greaterchi?refcode=trivianight0730). Every dollar of your donation goes to support Michael Feggans. 

### ABOUT THE RACE:
In 2023, Michael Feggans flipped House District 97 from a red to a blue seat in one of the most competitive races in Virginia and got right to work, earning the 2024 Climate All-Star Award from the Chesapeake Climate Action Network Fund and 2024 Legislative Rookie of the Year from the Virginia Education Association. Michael plans to continue his work in the House of Delegates serving the community he loves.

### ABOUT MICHAEL:
Michael Feggans was raised for most of his life in the West Kempsville portion of Virginia Beach. A proud product of the Virginia Beach Public School system, he graduated from Tallwood High School and immediately enlisted in the U.S. Air Force to pursue a career that would provide him the opportunity to become an innovative leader. An alumnus of VA Tech, Norfolk State, and UVA, he values and understands the importance of education, both traditional and nontraditional. After 20 years of service in the Air Force, he knew that the best place to retire from the military and start his next phase as a tech entrepreneur was back home in Virginia Beach.

title: NO KINGS! "We the People" Democracy Fair [Palo Alto]
description:
This Flag Day, join us for a democracy fair. Following a day of peaceful protests held in counterpoint to Donald Trump’s militaristic charade, we will host a celebration of what makes America truly great—and truly good. 

On June 14, we will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom. The democracy fair will be an occasion for people to convene after No Kings events being held across the Peninsula.

It will be an active, participatory gathering that includes something for everyone: an exhibit of pro-democracy art, music and theatrical performances on the theme of “No Kings,” tables where people can learn about activism opportunities, a Resistance Lab workshop, a costume competition (Elon Musk isn’t welcome, but Elon look-alikes might get a prize), and much more. 

This event—jointly sponsored by Bend the Arc, Indivisible Mid-Peninsula, Indivisible Palo Alto Plus, Indivisible Portola Valley, and It’s Blue Turn—will celebrate patriotism, not militarism. In saying NO to kings, we will also say YES to democracy.

The democracy fair will take place at Rinconada Park, and will follow a parade that starts at 2 p.m. The parade will begin at the intersection of El Camino Real and Embarcadero Road. description:
This free marshal training is being offered by Olive Action, a pro-democracy group that is part of the national Indivisible movement. Olive Action coordinates with Indivisible Ulster 18/19.

Marshaling is a form of resistance and democratic community building.  This 2-hour training covers the roles of marshals at a demonstration (a vigil, a legal picket, or a march through the streets) under the First Amendment, with an emphasis on de-escalating interactions with agitated protesters, the police, and counter-protesters.

Our goal is to create a safe, positive, and respectful learning space.
Anyone who plans to participate in an upcoming direct action is encouraged to take this training so we can build a reliable collective of trained marshals to call on.

title: 🎨 Civic Imagination: Why Creatives and Caregivers Belong in Government
description:
Join us for a conversation with Tom Tresser

What if the people shaping policy were the same ones shaping care, culture, and connection in our communities?

Join public theorist and commons defender Tom Tresser in this interactive conversation with Rochester artist and City Council candidate Kelly Cheatle as they explore why creatives and caregivers—those who tend to people and possibility—belong in the rooms where decisions are made.

We’ll talk about reclaiming public power, how civic imagination fuels real change, and what it takes to support community-rooted candidates—from donating and door knocking to simply showing up. Whether you’re a maker, a nurturer, or someone who believes in people-first leadership, this conversation is for you.

About Tom: 
Tom Tresser is a longtime organizer and educator who’s spent decades fighting for the public good. From blocking Chicago’s Olympic bid with No Games Chicago to leading campaigns for civic education and public ownership, Tom has dedicated his life to empowering everyday people to take back power from private interests.

He’s also co-founder of the CivicLab, a hub for civic imagination and training, and a fierce advocate for the creative and caregiving sectors as essential to democratic life. His latest effort, The 100K Project (www.100kproject.us) is a national movement to get 100,000 servant-leaders from the arts, nonprofit, nursing, library, education, science, and social work sectors to run for office (or to help someone run) as champions of service, science, justice, the rule of law, and creativity.

title: Flags Up! No Kings!
description:
**Saturday, June 14th (Flag Day)**, let us honor the true spirit of America: a nation where power belongs to the people, not to any single individual. Here in Ames, we invite all who cherish 'liberty and justice for ALL' to gather with us. Together, our voices will rise to defend our democracy and the enduring promise of freedom.

Join **Indivisible Ames** and **Democracy Every Day** for this vital community observance! To help share our patriotic spirit, we'll have **free American flags for participants** (limited numbers, so please come early to our main gathering!).

If you wish to **Volunteer** please contact *IndivisibleAmes@proton.me*

We are uniting as part of the **"No Kings" Nationwide Day of Defiance** to send an unmistakable message:

* No one is above the law.
* We demand accountability and cherish the rule of law.
* We will not stand idly by while our hard-won democratic freedoms – freedoms for everyone – are undermined.

### Here's what we're planning at Roosevelt Park (10:00 AM - 11:30 AM):

* **Gather & Connect (10:00 AM):** Meet us at **Roosevelt Park** for our main Flag Day morning gathering.

* **Inspiring Speakers (Lineup TBD):** Hear from passionate local voices and community leaders who are dedicated to protecting our democracy and advancing justice.
* ***Susan Benner***
    * Immigration Advocate
* *(More speakers to be announced!)*


**Optional Activity Following the Main Gathering:**

* **Flags Up! Mobile Sign Brigade (After Main Rally):** For those who wish to continue making our voices visible, an informal Mobile Sign Brigade will head out along Grand Ave. after our main program concludes. This is a great, energetic way to take our **"Flags Up! No Kings!"** message further into the community. Participation is optional – join if you're able!

## Why This Matters Right Now:

Our democratic republic, and the freedoms it promises, are not spectator sports; they require our active participation and unwavering defense from all of us. This Flag Day, let's demonstrate our collective strength, our resolve, and our commitment to a future where everyone's rights are protected, every voice matters, and the promise of American liberty is made real for all.

**RSVP now** to join **Indivisible Ames** and **Democracy Every Day** for **"Flags Up! No Kings!"** Be part of this crucial national day of action and let's send a clear message: **No Kings in America!**


## Guidelines for Rally Participants

### Our Approach: Be Respectful & Effective
Remember, a message delivered respectfully and without confrontation has the best chance of being heard. Always be polite and respectful, even to those who might disagree or try to engage negatively.
* *Do not engage in arguments. If someone yells at you from traffic, remember Michelle Obama's advice: "When they go low, we go high."*

### Safety First: Stick Together & Stay Aware
Never participate alone. For safety, always ensure you are with at least one other person. If you find yourself alone, call a friend to join you or return another day. Trust your instincts. If any interaction makes you feel uncomfortable or unsafe, disengage immediately, leave the area, and call the police if needed.

### Location & Conduct: Be Safe & Legal
Stay on public sidewalks or within the park. This is vital for everyone's safety (yours and drivers'), ensures pedestrians can pass (step into the park grass to let them by), and keeps us on legal public property. Public property includes sidewalks, the grassy area between the street and sidewalk (right-of-way), and city parks. Do not enter private property.
* *Keep yourself and your signs out of the street. Do not stand in the road or wave signs into traffic lanes.*
